metadata.title: Replication package for "Fully Autonomous Programming using Iterative Multi-Agent Debugging with Large Language Models"
metadata.description:
This repository contains the replication package for the paper Fully Autonomous Programming using Iterative Multi-Agent Debugging with Large Language Models, Anastasiia Grishina, Vadim Liventsev, Aki Härmä, and Leon Moonen, accepted for publication in ACM Transactions on Evolutionary Learning and Optimization with DOI: 10.1145/3719351

The replication package is archived on Zenodo with DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.13754705. The source code is distributed under the MIT license, the data is distributed under the CC BY 4.0 license.

Organization

The repository is organized as follows:

  • Archived source code in the src folder, with a dedicated README.

  • Analysis of the results in the analysis folder, with a dedicated README.

  • Archive of SEIDR-generated solutions as a git bundle: seidr-solutions.bundle.

    • These solutions can be inspected by cloning the bundle using git clone seidr-solutions.bundle which will create a folder seidr-solutions with a dedicated README in the master branch.
    • The other branches contain the code that was generated in specific experiments/configurations. List which experiments are available using git branch -r, select one using git checkout <branch>, and look at the iteratively synthesized solution for a problem using git log -p -- {problem}.{cpp/py}. Alternatively, these can be inspected on GitHub.

Citation

If you build on this data or code, please cite this work by referring to the paper:

@article{grishina2025:fully,
   title = {Fully Autonomous Programming using Iterative Multi-Agent Debugging with Large Language Models},
   author = {Anastasiia Grishina and Vadim Liventsev and Aki Härmä and Leon Moonen},
   journal = {Transactions on Evolutionary Learning and Optimization},
   year = {2025},
   publisher = {ACM}
   note = {Under review}
}

External References

  • The SEIDR source code is maintained on GitHub.
  • The SEIDR-generated solutions for PSB2 are versioned on GitHub as well.

metadata.title: Reproduction Package: Does the Tool Matter? Exploring Some Causes of Threats to Validity in Mining Software Repositories
metadata.description:
Study

The study uses the two mining software repositories (MSR) tools Codeface and Kaiaulu to extract and analyse ten large software projects, quantitatively and qualitatively comparing results and derived data to better understand the causes and impact of uncertainties in MSR tools and analysis pipelines.

The study can be reproduced based on our GitHub repository or this reproduction package.

 

Reproduction package

Due to the size limit of 50 GB, we cannot provide the fully self-contained docker image.

Instead, we provide all compressed artefacts and our study environment in the docker image separately.

The additional_material.zip may be inspected ad-hoc and is structured as follows:

  • analysis/: This directory contains all necessary bash scripts to reproduce our analysis pipeline as presented in the paper.
  • data/: This directory contains the git repositories and the data extracted by the MSR tools Codeface and Kaiaulu.
  • docker/: This directory contains the entrypoint script for the docker container.
  • log/: This directory contains log files of the comparative analysis scripts.
  • plot/: This directory contains the plots from the paper and the source code to generate them in R.
  • results/: This directory contains all results of the comparative analysis as CSV files.
  • src/: This directory contains our comparative analysis scripts in Python.
  • tools/: This directory contains the MSR tools Codeface and Kaiaulu with the configurations and adjustments described in the paper.

 

Reproduction setup

1. Import the docker image using 

docker load -i docker-image.tar.gz

2. Run a container from the image using

docker run --name saner -d -t --user saner saner

3. Unzip the additional_material.zip and copy the "db.sql" folder manually using

docker cp [local-path]/data/db.sql saner:/home/saner/data

4. Log in to the container using

docker exec -it saner bash

5. Import the MySQL database (password "codeface") using 

mysql -u codeface -p codeface < /home/saner/data/db.sql

 

Reproducing the analysis

We provide a single script to run all analysis steps from cloning git repositories, analysis with Codeface and Kaiaulu to baseline data and developer network comparisons.

Executing all analysis steps sequentially can be very time-consuming (up to several weeks) and risky due to sporadic parallelisation or database errors.

For quickly evaluating our replication package, you can exclude subject projects from the project_list in the /home/saner/analysis/analysis.conf in your docker container. The above script will then only consider the defined subset of projects. However, be aware that our visualisations are not optimised for this scenario.

If you prefer to analyse the entire set of subject projects with more control, or if you experience any errors, please refer to the "Important Notes" section below.

6. Start the study analysis pipeline in your docker container:

bash /home/saner/analysis/analysis.sh

7. When the analysis runs completed sucessfully, you can inspect the results on localhost with:

docker cp saner:/home/saner/data .
docker cp saner:/home/saner/log .
docker cp saner:/home/saner/plot .
docker cp saner:/home/saner/results .

metadata.title: Replication package for: LLMs for Generation of Architectural Components: An Exploratory Empirical Study in the Serverless World
metadata.description: This artifact presents a replication package for the ICSA 2025 submission titled "LLMs for Generation of Architectural Components: An Exploratory Empirical Study in the Serverless World" by Shrikara Arun*, Meghana Tedla*, Karthik Vaidhyanathan (* indicates equal contribution). This project investigates the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate architectural components, specifically focusing on Functions as a Service (FaaS), commonly referred to as serverless functions. By extending the scope of LLM-generated code from snippets to complete architectural components, this work introduces the potential to bridge design decisions directly to deployment, streamlining the software development process. This replication package is applying for the Research Object Reviewed (ROR) ROR-Functional, ROR Reusable and Open Research Object (ORO) badges. We are not applying for Results Validated badges (Results Reproduced (ROR-R) and Results Replicated (RER)) since we do not have independent researchers for verification nor is the reproduction of all results low effort. It involves significant investment in terms of time (execution and person hours) and non-zero cost to generate the serverless functions using the LLMs. This artifact contains the code for the automated steps in our study workflow, including: 1. filtering the Wonderless dataset for presence of tests & sorting based on GitHub stars and forks, 2. creating prompts, codebase summaries and serverless function descriptions using LLMs, 3. generating serverless functions using LLMs, 4. evaluating CodeBLEU and code metrics (LOC, cyclomatic and cognitive complexity and Halstead's volume) and 5. evaluating consistency of LLM generated serverless functions over multiple runs for the metrics previously mentioned. The artifact and instructions can be found at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14539783. Support is only provided for AMD64 Linux machines.

The LTPI Software Suite provides a comprehensive collection of tools and scripts to support the analysis, and visualization of results related to the LTPI manuscript. Key Features:

  1. Core Python code for LTPI analysis and simulations.
  2. Scripts to reproduce all figures and simulations presented in the LTPI manuscript.
    Includes modular and extensible code for figure generation and data analysis.
  3. Fully documented workflows with detailed instructions for running simulations and generating manuscript figures.

metadata.title: Replication package for Heat disproportionately kills young people: evidence from wet-bulb temperature in Mexico (Wilson et al., Science Advances, 2024)
metadata.description:
Description of the data and file structure

This repo contains scripts and data required to reproduce results in "Heat disproportionately kills young people: evidence from wet-bulb temperature in Mexico" with the exception of three pieces of data:

- Mexico's mortality microdata (this can be obtained at <https://en.www.inegi.org.mx/programas/edr/#microdata> and should be placed into the folder '../data/mortality/')
- Processed ERA5-Land reanalysis (this can be obtained by running the script at <https://code.earthengine.google.com/5f2337bbc6000ab5865429b2c8506ad9?noload=true> and storing the result in '../data/temps/era5/')
- Temperature projections data (which can be downloaded from <https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.qjq2bvqrc> and should then be stored in '../data/temps/projections/')

Files and variables

File: replication.zip

Description:  Contains all data and scripts necessary for complete reproduction. To reproduce all figures and tables, run all scripts in 'scripts/data_processing' in numerical order, then run all scripts in 'scripts/empirics' in numerical order. Before running each script, enter the location of the top-level directory for this repo into the 'setwd' command near the beginning of each script.

Subfolders

  • data
    Contains data necessary for reproducing results. Contains the following files and subfolders:
    • adm_dists.feather
      A compressed file storing distances between each municipality centroid and each weather station.
    • life_expectancy
      Contains a file with age-specific expected remaining life years from the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division World Population Prospects.
    • mortality
      Empty, but included as a location to store Mexico's mortality microdata (link in README description).
    • population
      Contains files describing the spatial distribution of people in Mexico, including from Facebook's High Resolution Population Density Maps and IPUMS International.
    • precip
      Contains population-weighted average precipitation exposure by municipality, as calculated in Google Earth Engine from ERA5-Land hourly data with weights provided by NASA SEDAC's Gridded Population of the World v. 4.11. A Google Earth Engine script to generate this data is available at https://code.earthengine.google.com/f2411f70f30bec8bdc0e1444d704fe3a.
    • shapefiles
      Shapefiles describing the borders of Mexico (from GADM.org), harmonized 1990 Mexican municipalities (from IPUMS International), and Mexico's climate classifications (from the World Bank, at https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0042325).
    • temps
      Contains the following folders:
      • era5
        Contains era5_global_max.nc, a record of global maximum hourly wet-bulb temperature by HadISD station, from https://github.com/cr2630git/raymondetal2020_sciadv
      • projections
      • station
        Historical weather observations for all stations in Mexico from HasISD, as well as station metadata.
  • output
    Empty, but included to hold results generated by running scripts.
  • scripts
    Contains code necessary for reproducing results. Contains the following subfolders:
    • data_processing
      Contains scripts that process and clean raw data.
    • empirics
      Contains scripts that produce results from processed and cleaned data.

Code/software

Reproduction requires the following R packages and their dependencies:

pacman v0.5.1

fastverse v0.3.2

tidyverse v2.0.0

lubridate v1.9.3

arrow v15.0.1

foreign v0.8-86

fixest v0.11.2

readxl v1.4.3

pammtools v0.5.93

scattermore v1.2

zoo v1.8-12

terra v1.7-71

sp v2.1-3

sf v1.0-15

exactextractr v0.10.0

cartogram v0.3.0

Analysis was completed using R version 4.3.0.
